z3r

Native R Interface to the Z3 Theorem Prover

z3r gives R direct access to Z3, the satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solver, through Z3’s C API. There is no Python, no reticulate, and no separate Z3 process: constraints are Z3 objects in memory, built with ordinary R operators.

library(z3r)

ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_int(ctx, "y")

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x + y == 10, x > 2 * y, y > 0)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_model(s)
#> <z3_model>
#>   y = 1
#>   x = 9

z3r is an independent third-party package. It is not developed, endorsed or supported by Microsoft or by the Z3 team.

What it covers

z3r targets Z3 5.4.1 (and works with every release from 4.8.13).

  • Theories: unbounded integers, exact reals and algebraic numbers, Booleans, bit-vectors, IEEE floating point, arrays, sets, strings, sequences, regular expressions, characters, algebraic datatypes, uninterpreted and recursive functions, quantifiers, special relations, pseudo-Boolean constraints, and the complex numbers, finite fields and finite sets of Z3 5.
  • Natural syntax: R operators (+ - * / ^ %/% %% == != < <= > >= & | !) with strict sort checking. Booleans are not numbers, bit-vectors never mix with unbounded integers, and R’s recycling rules never apply to formulas.
  • Solving: "sat", "unsat" and "unknown" kept distinct; models; push/pop and assumptions; unsatisfiable cores; proofs; consequences; cubes; timeouts and deterministic resource limits; Ctrl-C.
  • Optimization: objectives, weighted soft constraints, priorities, unbounded and non-attained optima reported as such.
  • Engines and tools: tactics, probes, simplifiers, constrained Horn clauses (Spacer) and Datalog, real closed fields, user propagators written in R, SMT-LIB2 import and export, and expression inspection and substitution.
  • Exact results: values come back as doubles only when exactly representable, otherwise as gmp numbers or exact strings.
  • Interoperability: exact translation to and from the symcompR computer algebra system.

Installation

z3r needs the Z3 C library and headers, version 4.8.13 or later (the first release with Z3’s Unicode string API). Nothing is downloaded during installation. Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 and Debian 12 ship Z3 4.8.12, which is too old; use a newer distribution package (Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04 ship 4.13.3) or an official release archive there. Features that need a newer Z3 than the one z3r was built with report so when they are called.

Any platform: an official release

Download the archive for your platform from the Z3 releases page (for example z3-5.4.1-arm64-osx-13.3.zip), unpack it, and point z3r at it:

Z3_INCLUDE_DIR=/path/to/z3-5.4.1/include Z3_LIB_DIR=/path/to/z3-5.4.1/bin \
  R -e 'remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/z3r")'

macOS 

brew install z3
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/z3r")

Verified with the official Z3 5.4.1 and 5.3.3 archives and with Homebrew’s Z3 4.16.0 on Apple silicon.

Linux 

sudo apt-get install libz3-dev    # Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04 or later
sudo dnf install z3-devel         # Fedora
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/z3r")

Verified on Ubuntu (arm64) with the distribution’s libz3-dev 4.13.3.

Windows

Download an official release such as z3-5.4.1-x64-win.zip from the Z3 releases page, unpack it, and point z3r at the unpacked folder:

Sys.setenv(Z3_DIR = "C:/path/to/z3-5.4.1-x64-win")
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/z3r")

Rtools links against libz3.dll directly, and the DLL is copied next to z3r’s own DLL. The Windows build is written and covered by the CI workflow, but it has not been run on Windows yet.

Choosing a specific Z3

The configure script looks, in order, at PKG_CPPFLAGS/PKG_LIBS, at Z3_INCLUDE_DIR/Z3_LIB_DIR (or Z3_DIR on Windows), at pkg-config z3, and at the usual prefixes (/opt/homebrew, /usr/local, /usr). It links the chosen library by its full path and refuses headers and libraries of different versions:

Z3_INCLUDE_DIR=/opt/z3/include Z3_LIB_DIR=/opt/z3/bin R CMD INSTALL z3r

z3_version() reports the library z3r runs with and the headers it was compiled against.

CRAN

z3r is not on CRAN. A CRAN release needs a Z3 binary for CRAN’s Windows and macOS builders, which requires coordinating with the CRAN maintainers of the build toolchains (Rtools and the macOS recipes); this has not been done.

Learning more

The website has the full reference and seventeen articles, from vignette("z3r") (SMT solving for R users) to one article per theory and engine: exact numbers, solving, optimization, logic puzzles, bit-vectors, floating point, arrays and sets, strings and regular expressions, datatypes, functions and quantifiers, tactics, Horn clauses, algebraic numbers, SMT-LIB2 and inspection, user propagators, the Z3 5 theories, and symcompR.
